label: Diagram 3
caption: Diagram 3 Requirement RA1 – a. schematic example where gigabit-ready physical infrastructure is installed from a network termination point to a point as close as is reasonably practicable to a likely future location for a network distribution point, and b. schematic example where, due to the absence of a likely future location for a network distribution point, and a lack of developer access rights, gigabit-ready physical infrastructure is built from the network termination point to the access point or common access point only
description:
This diagram, headed Diagram 3 under Requirement RA1, has two schematic drawings, a and b, with a legend at the right of part a. The legend defines the green shaded area as land to which the developer has access to install infrastructure, the dashed square as likely future network distribution points, the grey square as a dwelling/building containing more than one dwelling, and a symbol of an open circle joined by a vertical line to a smaller open circle as gigabit-ready physical infrastructure.

In part a, two grey squares lie side by side within the green area. A label above, 'Network termination point (one each per dwelling in building)', points with a leader line to the open circle inside the left grey square, and each grey square contains one such open circle with a short line running down from it to a small open rectangle at the bottom of the square. The two rectangles are joined by a line, which is labelled 'Access point/ common access point'. From this line a further line runs down and then to the left, ending at a small open rectangle on the left of the green area, labelled 'Point as close as is reasonably practicable to a location at which a distribution point is likely to be installed within the relevant 2-year period (a 'likely future location')'. Above this rectangle is a dashed square, labelled 'Location at which a distribution point is likely to be installed within the relevant 2-year period (a 'likely future location')', with no line connecting to it.

In part b the same green area contains the same two grey squares, each with its open circle and line to a bottom rectangle, the two rectangles joined by a line labelled 'Access point/ common access point'; no line leads out of the green area and there is no dashed square or left-hand rectangle. A boxed inset on the left shows a single grey square containing two open circles joined by a line to a small open rectangle at the bottom, with the caption: 'Inset: in-building infrastructure example. In this case, network termination points for two dwellings connect inside the building to a common access point.'
